title: satureja punctata subsp. ovata
intro: Satureja punctata subsp. ovata, commonly known as Iranian savory, is a plant species belonging to the Lamiaceae family, characterized by its small, ovate leaves and purple flowers. The plant has been traditionally used in folk medicine to treat various health issues, including digestive problems, respiratory infections, and skin conditions, due to its numerous health benefits. Its therapeutic actions are attributed to its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties, which may help to reduce inflammation, improve wound healing, and prevent the growth of pathogens. The bioactive constituents of Iranian savory include volatile oils, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, such as carvacrol, thymol, and rosmarinic acid, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
